evidence: src/domain/repositories/ProjectRepository.ts: `interface ProjectRepository { save(project: Project): Promise<void>; findById(id: string): Promise<Project | undefined>; }`. A persistence port for the Project aggregate.

src/domain/repositories/TaskRepository.ts: `interface TaskRepository` has the same save/findById shape plus `findByProject(projectId, criteria: TaskCriteria)`. `TaskCriteria { status?: TaskStatus; assigneeId?: string }` is a query object used only by this repository.
src/domain/repositories/UserRepository.ts: `interface UserRepository { save(user: User): Promise<void>; findById(id: string): Promise<User | undefined>; }`. Same port convention as the other two.

Graph: application use cases depend on these interfaces through CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edges, and infrastructure InMemory* classes implement them (IMPLEMENTS edges). That fits one coherent port boundary.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This module passes. All three files serve one concern: they are the domain's persistence interfaces (ports), one for each aggregate (Project, Task, User). All three follow the same pattern: save(entity): Promise<void> and findById(id): Promise<Entity | undefined>. Each depends only on its own domain entity, plus a value object in the Task case. TaskCriteria is a query object used only by TaskRepository.findByProject, so it belongs in TaskRepository.ts. It does not repeat a rule that lives elsewhere. No business rule or invariant is written into more than one file, and nothing works around the module's own abstractions: each file contains only interface declarations. The shared save/findById shape is a deliberate convention, not a duplicated invariant. Nothing in the material shows it should be pulled into a common generic base.
